segments.text: 18-річний хлопець на ім'я Джордж-молодший проїхав че́рез своє рідне місто
segments.original: An 18-year-old boy named George Jr. drove through his hometown on his way home for dinner.

segments.text: Але́ у той момент, коли́ ві́н їхав. Джордж-молодший відчути
segments.original: But as he was driving, George Jr. could not help but feel like he was really dreading actually getting there.

segments.text: Джордж-молодший був ду́же розумною дитиною. але́ ві́н тако́ж ду́же легко відволікався
segments.original: So George Jr. was a very smart kid, but he also got distracted really easily, and because of that he really had not pursued anything all that seriously, that is except for cars.

segments.text: І в той момент його́ батько дійсно купив йому маленьку італійську машину під назвою Фіат. але́ його́ батько
segments.original: And at that point his father actually bought him a small Italian car called a Fiat, but his father, despite being the one who literally gave him the Fiat, he just didn't get his son's obsession with cars.

segments.text: Наприклад, чому ви не можете зосередитися на цьому й застосувати його до інших речей, які дадуть вам справжню роботу?
segments.original: Like why aren't you able to take that focus and apply it to other things that will get you a real job?

segments.text: І тому́ практично кожна вечеря в ці дні перетворювалася на величезну суперечку між батьком і сином
segments.original: And so basically every dinner these days it became this huge argument between father and son.

segments.text: І ось Джордж. ві́н підійшов до цього перехрестя. де воно бу́ло прямо біля його́ дому
segments.original: And so George, he came to this intersection where it was right near his home

segments.text: і ві́н почав повертати.
segments.original: and he begins making the turn when he hears this really loud screeching sound and then everything went black.

segments.text: Че́рез два тижні Джордж-молодший лежав у реанімації місцевої лікарні. тож за два тижні до того. у той момент, коли́ Джордж робив поворот. а по́тім щось трапилося
segments.original: Two weeks later, George Jr. was laying in a hospital bed in the intensive care unit at the local hospital, so two weeks earlier when George was making that turn and then something happened, well what it was is another car came speeding down the road and smashed into George's car so hard that George Jr. was ejected from the car, but he had survived.

segments.text: Че́рез два роки Джордж-молодший. яки́й до цього моменту вже́ повністю оговтався від травм
segments.original: Two years later, George Jr., who by this point was fully recovered from his injuries, stood at the finish line at a race track and raised his camera.

segments.text: Тож пі́сля свого передсмертного досвіду Джордж-молодший зрозумів, досвід на межі смерті.
segments.original: So since his near-death experience, George Jr. had realized that really his dad had been kind of right, that in some ways he was wasting his potential.

segments.text: Тож Джордж-молодший вирішив. що справді бі́льше не хоче брати участь у перегонах автомобілів
segments.original: So George Jr. had decided that he really didn't want to race cars anymore. Instead he had picked up his camera and really gotten back into his old hobby of photography.

segments.text: Насправді Джордж-молодший подав заявку на престижну програму кінематографії в Ю Ес Сі. але́ пі́сля того
segments.original: In fact, George Jr. had applied to the prestigious cinematography program at the University of Southern California, but after sending off his application, he was pretty sure he would not get in.

segments.text: Тепер Джордж-молодший підійшов до подіуму. щоб зробити декілька фотографій водія-переможця
segments.original: Now, George Jr. walked over to the podium to take some photos of the winning driver, but as he walked over there, this middle-aged man came up beside him and just asked George Jr. about his photography.

segments.text: І тоді́ в якийсь момент цей чоловік фактично офіційно представився як Хаскелл Векслер і сказав
segments.original: And then at some point, the man actually formally introduced himself as Haskell Wexler and he said that he was actually a cinematographer in Hollywood.

segments.text: І Джордж-молодший розповів Хаскеллу про те
segments.original: And George Jr. told Haskell about how he had recently applied to USC to try to get into their cinematography program.

segments.text: І у той момент, у той момент, коли́ Хаскелл почув це
segments.original: And when Haskell heard this, he said, George, I know people at USC.

segments.text: Дозволь мені подзвонити. І справді
segments.original: Let me make some calls. And sure enough, not long after this fateful meeting, George Jr. would receive an acceptance letter from USC's film school.

segments.text: Але́ цей момент у житті Джорджа-молодшого не лише змінив його́ життя назавжди
segments.original: But this moment in George Jr.'s life did not just alter George's life forever.

segments.text: Це тако́ж назавжди повністю змінило б кіно в цілому
segments.original: It also would go on to completely alter cinema in general forever. Because about 13 years later, George Jr. would go on to create one of the most groundbreaking films in history.

segments.text: Його́ фільм став частиною найуспішнішої кінофраншизи всіх часів
segments.original: His movie would go on to become part of the most successful movie franchise of all time.

source_segments: An 18-year-old boy named George Jr. drove through his hometown on his way home for dinner.
But as he was driving, George Jr. could not help but feel like he was really dreading actually getting there.
So George Jr. was a very smart kid, but he also got distracted really easily, and because of that he really had not pursued anything all that seriously, that is except for cars.

And at that point his father actually bought him a small Italian car called a Fiat, but his father, despite being the one who literally gave him the Fiat, he just didn't get his son's obsession with cars.
Like why aren't you able to take that focus and apply it to other things that will get you a real job?
And so basically every dinner these days it became this huge argument between father and son.
And so George, he came to this intersection where it was right near his home
and he begins making the turn when he hears this really loud screeching sound and then everything went black.

Two weeks later, George Jr. was laying in a hospital bed in the intensive care unit at the local hospital, so two weeks earlier when George was making that turn and then something happened, well what it was is another car came speeding down the road and smashed into George's car so hard that George Jr. was ejected from the car, but he had survived.
Two years later, George Jr., who by this point was fully recovered from his injuries, stood at the finish line at a race track and raised his camera.
So since his near-death experience, George Jr. had realized that really his dad had been kind of right, that in some ways he was wasting his potential.
So George Jr. had decided that he really didn't want to race cars anymore. Instead he had picked up his camera and really gotten back into his old hobby of photography.
In fact, George Jr. had applied to the prestigious cinematography program at the University of Southern California, but after sending off his application, he was pretty sure he would not get in.

Now, George Jr. walked over to the podium to take some photos of the winning driver, but as he walked over there, this middle-aged man came up beside him and just asked George Jr. about his photography.
And then at some point, the man actually formally introduced himself as Haskell Wexler and he said that he was actually a cinematographer in Hollywood.
And George Jr. told Haskell about how he had recently applied to USC to try to get into their cinematography program.
And when Haskell heard this, he said, George, I know people at USC.
Let me make some calls. And sure enough, not long after this fateful meeting, George Jr. would receive an acceptance letter from USC's film school.
But this moment in George Jr.'s life did not just alter George's life forever.
It also would go on to completely alter cinema in general forever. Because about 13 years later, George Jr. would go on to create one of the most groundbreaking films in history.
His movie would go on to become part of the most successful movie franchise of all time.
George Jr. is better known today as George Lucas, and his film franchise was Star Wars. and his film franchise was Star Wars.
